solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dazzlingly bright indeed, in shimmering gold

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, sitting within its letters
something shimmering flickers and shifts, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
ay is an old or dialect word for yes, indeed

explanation.surface: Something glittering in gold is described as brilliantly bright.
explanation.definitionFit: Day-Glo is a trademark name for fluorescent paint and colours, so it describes something glaringly vivid.

clue.text: On-line trader from Thailand caught in ruin

indicators.note: something caught in a thing is trapped inside it, so the earlier letters go within

parts.note: doom is ruin or destruction
T is the international vehicle code for Thailand
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An internet business from Thailand is brought down by financial collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' does double duty in the surface but here it is just the letter C, and 'in' then places T and C inside the word for ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: A dotcom is a company that does its business over the internet, an online trader.

clue.text: Middle-easterner, independence overcome by revolutionary enemy

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece overcome by another lies beneath it, so it comes second
a revolutionary overturns the existing order, so the following word's letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
I is a standard abbreviation for independent or independence

explanation.surface: A Middle Eastern figure sees his country's independence crushed by a rebel foe.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged word is the country itself, and the extra I turns the country into its native.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yemeni is a native of Yemen, a country in the Arabian peninsula in the Middle East.

clue.text: Noble name and lineage gets you this? (12, two words)

definitions.text: Noble name and lineage gets you this?

parts.note: a grandee is a nobleman of the highest rank, especially in Spain
n is the abbreviation for name
a family tree sets out a lineage

explanation.surface: A question of what an aristocratic name and pedigree will earn you.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the recipe and the definition: being a titled person of good family is exactly what got you privileged admission at court.
explanation.definitionFit: A grande entrée is the right of entry to a royal court, a privilege that rank and pedigree would secure.

clue.text: They help to protect you at home as part of titular estate

definitions.text: They help to protect you at home

indicators.note: the answer is only a part of the phrase that follows, sitting within its letters

parts.note: found across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Talk of guardians who look after you at home on a titled family's estate.
explanation.walkthrough: The run of letters straddles the gap between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lares were Roman household gods, guardian spirits who watched over the home and family.

clue.text: Gay lot raving, a threat to audition?

indicators.note: raving means wild and deranged, so the letters before it are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A merry crowd partying loudly could damage your hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Audition' looks like a tryout for a show; here it means the faculty of hearing, which an earache threatens.
explanation.definitionFit: Otalgy is the medical term for earache, a pain that could impair the sense of hearing.

clue.text: Bribe old copper, in favour no longer

indicators.note: the first piece sits inside the second, within its letters

parts.note: gree is an obsolete word for goodwill or favour, hence no longer
the as was an ancient Roman coin made of copper or bronze

explanation.surface: An old policeman bribed, then dropped out of favour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman, but the old copper is a Roman coin.
explanation.definitionFit: To grease someone's palm is to bribe them, so grease alone works as a verb for bribing.

clue.text: Old tom suffered what's made of offal

parts.note: gib is an old word for a tomcat, especially a castrated one
to suffer in the old sense is to allow or let

explanation.surface: An old cat put up with being fed offal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suffered' looks like pain, but it is the old sense of permitted.
explanation.definitionFit: A giblet is one of the edible internal organs of a bird, which together make up its offal.

clue.text: A Latin poem I composed about husband, it was performed at marriage

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters wrap around the other piece
something composed is put together, so these letters are assembled in another order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
h is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A poet recounts writing a Latin poem about a husband that was recited at a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's poem is real: the answer is that kind of poem, built from a rearranged 'A Latin poem I' around the husband.
explanation.definitionFit: An epithalamion is a song or poem in honour of a bride and bridegroom, sung or read at a wedding.

clue.text: One fib admitted by civic dignitary briefly

indicators.note: what is admitted by something is let in, so the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: Ald is the short form of alderman, a civic dignitary
a fib is a small lie

explanation.surface: A single small untruth is owned up to by a local councillor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' looks like a number counting fibs; it is the definition, meaning united.
explanation.definitionFit: Allied parties are joined together, so they act as one; 'one' here means united.

clue.text: Specific soil type alone surmounting difficulties

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece surmounting another sits on top of it, so it comes first

parts.note: solo means alone
nets are snares or entanglements, things that cause difficulty

explanation.surface: A particular kind of soil overcomes problems by itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Solonets (or solonetz) is a dark alkaline soil type formed when salts are leached, a technical soil-science name.

clue.text: Pollen membranes displaying oomph when coating's removed?

indicators.note: a coating is the outside layer, so the first and last letters are stripped away

parts.note: oomph is sex appeal, sexiness

explanation.surface: Pollen membranes suddenly look appealing once their coating is peeled off.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the coating means dropping the outer letter at each end of the word for oomph.
explanation.definitionFit: The exine is the tough outer wall of a pollen grain or spore, so exines are pollen membranes.

clue.text: Vaguely histrionic eye admitting age

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the next piece goes inside the first

parts.note: optic is a word for the eye
an era is an age

explanation.surface: A rather theatrical eye lets in a period of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Operatic behaviour is melodramatic and overdone like grand opera, so somewhat histrionic.

clue.text: Dine with this? A marinated mix possibly

definitions.text: Dine with this? A marinated mix possibly

indicators.note: to mix is to jumble, so the letters before it are reordered
the answer is what goes with the named word to make up the mixed letters, so that word is taken away from them

parts.note: taken as written, the full set of letters to be rearranged
taken as written, the letters to be removed from the mix

explanation.surface: A suggestion of what to eat: a dish soaked in marinade, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: DINE plus the answer is a reshuffle of A MARINATED, so the answer is what remains once DINE is subtracted; the whole clue doubles as its definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamara is a spice mixture of cinnamon, cloves, coriander and other seasonings, something you might cook and eat with.

clue.text: Magistrate? I'll follow one in written accusation

indicators.note: read as I will follow, so the letter I is added after the rest
one piece placed in another sits within its letters

parts.note: a bill of indictment is a written accusation
a means one
taken as written, from the contraction I'll

explanation.surface: A magistrate says he will come after someone named in a charge sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'll follow' reads as 'I will follow': the letter I goes after A placed inside BILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A bailli was a magistrate or bailiff in France and the Channel Islands, an administrator of justice.

clue.text: Battlement thing made to protect Eleanor?

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround and shield it, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: a creation is something made
Nell is a pet form of the name Eleanor

explanation.surface: A defensive wall is built to keep a queen called Eleanor safe.
explanation.walkthrough: The name has to be shortened to its familiar form before it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Crenellation is the notched parapet on a castle wall, made of battlements with gaps for firing.

clue.text: My rooms have adjacent parking — I let more converted

indicators.note: converting something turns it into another form, so these letters take another order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A landlord boasts that his rooms come with a car park beside them, so he lets more.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the speaker describing himself, a fitting picture for someone who lets rooms beside parked cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A motelier runs a motel, roadside lodging where guests park right outside their rooms.

clue.text: Faraday's discovery penned in monograph en effet

indicators.note: penned in means enclosed, so the answer is enclosed within the words that follow

parts.note: found running across the three words

explanation.surface: A scientific discovery written up in a learned monograph, in effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'En effet' is French for 'in effect', there to give the hidden run its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Phene is an old name for benzene, which Michael Faraday first isolated in 1825.

clue.text: Half, i.e. time in second year

indicators.note: the first pieces go in, that is inside, the letters that follow

parts.note: mo is a moment, a second
taken as written, without the stops
t is the abbreviation for time
y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A note that half means this much time within a second year.
explanation.definitionFit: A moiety is one of two equal parts, a half share, as in legal language.

clue.text: Winds from south-east nip back

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the whole string is read from its end

parts.note: SE is the compass abbreviation
to nip is to dash or dart

explanation.surface: Winds blowing in from the south-east give a quick nip on the way back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winds' looks like a verb, but it is the noun for steady tropical airflows.
explanation.definitionFit: The trades are the trade winds, steady winds blowing towards the equator from the north-east and south-east.

clue.text: I'm turned off teacher possibly — it's the pressure

indicators.note: turned means facing the other way, so the two letters are taken backwards
off means taken away from, so those letters are removed from the following word

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
a schoolmistress is a teacher, so mistress is one example

explanation.surface: Someone driven away from teaching says the strain was the cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' flags that mistress is only one kind of teacher, as in a schoolmistress.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is pressure or strain, whether physical force or mental tension.

clue.text: Plug post, one assumes? (6, two words)

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to block or close an opening
second meaning: to stay out of bed late, as one presumes a sentry at a post does

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the colloquial one of not going to bed; the question mark admits that someone on watch at a post is only presumed to stay awake.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to block a hole completely and, informally, to remain awake late into the night.

clue.text: Including a dash of enzlan, give fresh colour to cheap whiskey

indicators.note: including means taking in, so the other piece goes inside

parts.note: to re-dye is to colour something again

indicators.note: a dash is a tiny amount, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the first letter of the word for a gentian liqueur, as printed

explanation.surface: Adding a drop of gentian liqueur gives rough whiskey a new colour.
explanation.walkthrough: Enzian is a German gentian spirit (printed here as 'enzlan'); only its first letter matters. Whiskey spelt with an E points to American usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Redeye is US slang for cheap, raw whiskey, named for its supposed effect on the drinker's eyes.

clue.text: Discovers local rate going up around the States

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the first piece wraps the second
in a down entry, going up means read from bottom to top, so the letters are taken backwards

parts.note: sess or cess is a Scottish and Irish word for a local tax or rate
US is the abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: Someone finds out that council tax is rising across America.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local rate' is a British council tax; the regional word for it here is sess.
explanation.definitionFit: To suss something out is informal British slang for working it out or discovering it.

clue.text: Acrobatic feat? One's bananas to produce such!

definitions.text: Acrobatic feat? One's bananas to produce such!

parts.note: surface reading: a gymnastic move where the legs go out flat in opposite directions
setter's reading: a fruit dessert is made by slicing bananas lengthwise, and 'bananas' also means crazy

explanation.surface: Only someone crazy would attempt such an acrobatic move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' reads as slang for mad, but it is the fruit: you need bananas to make the ice-cream dessert of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a gymnast's leg stretch along the floor and, with banana, an ice-cream sundae.

clue.text: Drunk bowler? If only (6, two words)

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard
a bowler is a hard round hat

explanation.surface: Someone wishes a cricketer were tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowler' points to cricket, but it is the hat.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase can mean provided that or on condition that, the conditional sense of 'if only'.

clue.text: What'll provide sport in Nice? That's crazy (6, two words)

definitions.text: What'll provide sport in Nice? That's crazy

indicators.note: the first piece is placed in the second, within its letters
crazy means deranged, so the letters of the town are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
RU is the abbreviation for Rugby Union

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of a winter-sports facility in balmy Nice.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a track for sliding sports on the warm Riviera would indeed be crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice run is a frozen track for tobogganing or sledging, built to give sport.

clue.text: I spy!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the person who wrote this clue speaking of themself
second meaning: an informer or decoy who sets someone up

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as the children's game, but 'I' is the compiler and 'spy' is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The compiler of the puzzle is its setter, and in old slang a setter is a spy or police informer.

clue.text: Poet's to inflame young adult with start of desire

parts.note: a teen is a teenager, a young adult

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A poet wants to fire up a youngster with the beginnings of longing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poet's' marks the word as poetic and archaic, used by Spenser.
explanation.definitionFit: Teend is a Spenserian verb meaning to kindle or set alight, so to inflame.

clue.text: Neighbours of S Claus? One among the aforesaid

indicators.note: something among others is placed in their midst, so it goes inside

parts.note: the same means the thing already mentioned
a means one

explanation.surface: A question about who lives near Santa, answered with one of those just mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: Santa Claus is said to live in Lapland, home of these reindeer-herding people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Saame (Sami) are the indigenous people of Lapland, where legend places Santa Claus's home.

clue.text: Job's place, diversifying modest talent (12, two words)

indicators.note: diversifying means varying, so the letters are made to vary in order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An employer broadens a workplace's modest skills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Job' is not employment but the biblical Job, whose book is in the Hebrew scriptures.
explanation.definitionFit: The Book of Job is part of the Old Testament, the first section of the Christian Bible.

clue.text: Butterflies? One may be seen in proms

indicators.note: something seen in a place is inside it, so the first piece sits within the second

parts.note: proms are promenades, and seaside piers are walkways of that kind
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A butterfly might be spotted at a promenade concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proms' suggests the concerts but means seaside promenades. The question mark admits the answer is a genus, not butterflies in general.
explanation.definitionFit: Pieris is the genus of the cabbage white butterflies, so it names a group of butterflies.

clue.text: Tattie-howking? One's involved with this around summer's end

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the word wraps the single letter
involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed together

parts.note: a means one
taken as written

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, which is the one kept

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: A Scot digging potatoes is involved in this work at the end of summer.
explanation.walkthrough: Tattie-howking is Scots for lifting potatoes, a harvest job; the answer is Scots too, and the question mark shows the definition is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairst is Scots for harvest, and potato-lifting is one kind of harvest work.

clue.text: Bristly worm in stratum alongside river (8, two words)

indicators.note: alongside means placed next to, so the two pieces sit side by side in order

parts.note: a seam is a layer or stratum, as of coal
the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: A hairy worm found in a rock layer next to a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is the name of several English rivers, including the one through York.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea mouse is a marine worm covered in iridescent bristles, giving it a furry mouselike look.

clue.text: Grooms? Silly person, one of three in engagement losing ring

indicators.note: silly means foolish and muddled, so the letters are jumbled
losing something means it is taken away from the letters

parts.note: taken as written
the word engagement contains three of this letter
o is a ring shape

explanation.surface: Wedding grooms in question: a fool in a three-way engagement who has lost the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly person' looks like a fool, but 'Silly' is the signal and 'person' the letters; the ring is dropped and the E added before mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: To groom is to tidy one's appearance, and to preen is to smarten oneself up, so grooms and preens are verb synonyms.

clue.text: Name new modified tree rings for decade

indicators.note: something that rings another encircles it, so the word goes around the letters
modified means altered, so the letters take another order

parts.note: n is the abbreviation for new
taken as written, to be rearranged
n is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A new kind of tree whose growth rings mark ten years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tenner' usually means a ten-pound note; here it is a span of ten years.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenner can be anything comprising ten, including a ten-year period or sentence.
